content_html:
Gum is easier to remove once it is no longer soft and sticky. Chilling it lets you lift away most of the material without spreading it; remaining residue can then be treated with a fabric-compatible product, with heat avoided until the stain is gone.

Chill the gum until it hardens

Hold ice in a bag against the area or, if practical, chill the garment in the freezer without contaminating food. Once the gum is hard, work from the edges instead of stretching it across the fabric.

Lift the solid gum with a dull edge

Use a spoon or dull card to separate the gum little by little. Avoid blades and aggressive scraping, especially on knits, thin garments, or delicate finishes.

Treat residue with a compatible product

A liquid detergent or stain remover approved for the fiber can help with the sticky film. Test first in an inconspicuous area and do not mix solvents or improvise with products that may remove color.

Inspect before using heat

Wash according to the care label and inspect before drying. If the area still feels tacky or a mark remains, repeat treatment; dryer heat can make the remaining residue harder to remove.
